name: model-router
description: Haiku sorts every subagent task into simple, standard, hard or long run and picks the model; a pane shows what each agent cost.

baseline.title: Compare against
baseline.description: What the bill pane prices the same tokens on, to show what routing saved. unrouted: the model each agent would have run on without the router (its parent's), so the main conversation saves nothing

routeAll.title: Route every subagent
routeAll.description: On: route built-in subagents (Explore, general-purpose) too. Off: only the four router agents.

respectExplicitModel.title: Keep a model Claude asked for
respectExplicitModel.description: On: when the Agent call already names a model, leave it alone

effortByTier.title: Lower effort for easy tasks
effortByTier.description: On: a simple task's subagent thinks at low effort and a standard one at medium at most. Hard and long tasks keep the effort they had, and an Agent call that sets its own effort keeps it

riskFloor.title: Send risky tasks to Opus
riskFloor.description: On: a task whose act could do costly or hard-to-reverse harm (deploying to production, deleting data, a forced push) runs on Opus at least, whatever its role or the rate limits

limitPressure.title: Route cheaper near rate limits
limitPressure.description: When the fullest rate-limit window (5-hour or weekly) is at this percent or more, route one tier lower and never to Fable. off: ignore rate limits
